uncited: This family categorizes direct volume ray casting methods by their specific data storage formats (e.g., 3D textures, fixed-point grids) and the integrators used to process them.

It distinguishes between GPU-native texture-based ray marching and CPU-optimized fixed-point arithmetic, addressing performance bottlenecks in memory bandwidth and computational precision for large-scale datasets.

All methods in this family adhere to the core mechanism of [Direct volume ray casting](19-direct-volume-ray-casting.md): defining rays, sampling volume data, classifying via transfer functions, and compositing using front-to-back integration.
The divergence lies in the data representation (texture vs. grid) and the arithmetic precision (floating-point vs. fixed-point) used during sampling and accumulation.
The use of 3D textures for ray marching became standard with the advent of programmable GPUs and WebGL2, allowing direct access to volumetric data without intermediate geometry .
